cards.explanation: The answer is that they obey the voice of the LORD. Zerubbabel, Joshua and all the remnant of the people "…obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of the prophet Haggai…" (Haggai 1:12). They hear it, and they obey, friends.

The word is sent. The people obeyed Haggai's words "…because the LORD their God had sent him." (Haggai 1:12). They didn't hear one man's opinion, friends. They heard a messenger with a message from the LORD, and they treated it that way.

The LORD says, "I am with you…" (Haggai 1:13). Haggai delivers those four little words to the people who just obeyed. I think that's about the best thing you could hear right when you're about to roll up your sleeves, friends.

The answer is the LORD. "…the LORD stirred the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah…" (Haggai 1:14). Notice who does the stirring, bakers. The governor didn't pump himself up with a speech in the mirror.

The answer is False. The LORD stirred the spirit of Zerubbabel, and also the spirit of Joshua the high priest and "…the spirit of all the remnant of the people." (Haggai 1:14). Nobody got left on the sidelines, friends. Governor, priest and people all get stirred.

The word is begin. The text says "…they came and began the work on the house of the LORD of Hosts, their God…" (Haggai 1:14). The LORD had called His house a ruin (Haggai 1:9), and now the work on it starts. Every big job has a first day, bakers, and this is theirs.
The answer is King Darius. The work begins "…in the second year of King Darius." (Haggai 1:15). The text pins down the day and the year, friends, and I love a passage that keeps good records.
